title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.

steps.action: Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
Pick a new number and remember it.
Act from the revision, not the original alarm.

win: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
supports: Exhale after “Follow Evidence”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Check Baseline” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Score Odds → Check Baseline → Weigh Evidence → Revise Odds → Follow Evidence
safety:
PAUSE
End the count if numbers become reassurance checking or you cannot stop recalculating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
goal: Authority often hides inside delivery.

steps.action: Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.

win: ✓ A fixed rule turned back into a context-dependent idea.
supports: I can use “Keep Words” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Read Wrong → Keep Words → Replay
safety:
PAUSE
Use a neutral voice instead if playful recasting feels shaming or agitating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
goal: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.

steps.action: Project the sentence on an inner screen.
Shrink it to caption size.
Move it two metres away.
Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.

win: ✓ The thought changed format, and some of its spell broke.
supports: Exhale after “Read Version”; loosen the label.
I can use “Shrink” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Project → Shrink → Move Metres → Lower Opacity → Read Version
safety:
PAUSE
Return to external grounding if visual manipulation feels unreal or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
goal: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.

steps.action: State what moved off course in plain language.
Remove every adjective about your character.
Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.

win: ✓ Re-entry happened without opening a courtroom.
supports: Exhale after “Skip Verdict”; keep the compass.
I can use “Delete Adjectives” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: State Off → Delete → Name Value → Move Whether → Skip Verdict
safety:
PAUSE
Address repeated harmful drift with accountability and support, not endless self-restarts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TENSION’S EXIT PARTNER
goal: Teach one muscle where release lives.

steps.action: Select a safe body region.
Tighten it lightly—not maximally—during an easy inhale.
As air leaves, let the muscle become heavy and wide.
Compare before and after, then move to a second region only if the first fully released.
One clean contrast is enough.

win: ✓ I felt one clean contrast and stopped before turning it into a test.
supports: Gently exhale after “End Clean”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Tighten” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Select Safe → Tighten → Leave Muscle → Compare After → End Clean
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid injured, painful, recently operated, or cramping areas.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIVE SAFE SIGNALS
goal: Send calm through more than one doorway.

steps.action: Build a sensory sequence from what is available: one pleasing sight, steady sound, comforting texture, mild scent, and nourishing taste.
Spend a few seconds receiving each instead of rushing to the next cue.
End on the sense that feels most trustworthy today.

win: ✓ The clock stopped voting louder than the facts.
supports: Exhale after “End Sense”; slow the clock.
I can use “Receive Instead” without rushing.
formula_flow: Build Sensory → Receive Instead → End Sense
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid allergens, unsafe temperatures, substance triggers, or sensory input that overwhelms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DROP THE APPEAL
goal: Reality has already entered the room; the appeal is only in your mind.

steps.action: State the fact in plain past or present tense.
Remove approval, blame, and every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the body’s protest and answer, ‘Not liking it is allowed.
Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.

win: ✓ I stopped appealing reality and moved inside the version that exists.
supports: Exhale after “Add Nothing”; release extra blame.
I can use “Remove Approval” without owning everything.
formula_flow: State Fact → Remove Approval → Add Nothing
safety:
PAUSE
Acceptance must never be used to legitimise abuse, injustice, or preventable harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN AGAIN
goal: Acceptance is often a direction repeated, not a mood achieved.

steps.action: Catch the mind reopening the case against what has already occurred.
Name the refusal without criticism.
Rotate attention toward the existing fact and the action now possible.
Each return is one turn of the wheel; stop counting after the chosen behaviour begins.

win: ✓ I turned back toward reality once more—and stopped counting when action began.
supports: Exhale after “Return Wheel”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Name Refusal” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Catch Mind → Name Refusal → Rotate Attention → Return Wheel
safety:
PAUSE
If repeated turning becomes compulsive, step away and use ordinary support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR
goal: Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.

steps.action: Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’

win: ✓ Good got a place on the calendar without needing a score.
supports: Exhale after “Lock It In”; let feeling settle.
“Choose Genuinely” versus “Lock It In”: what eased?
I can use “Protect Appointment” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose Genuinely → Protect Appointment → Details → Lock It In
safety:
PAUSE
Do not force pleasure during grief or depression; attendance itself can be the result.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE SENSATION
goal: Teach the body that a safe signal is not the worst-case story.

steps.action: Select a medically safe exercise that creates a mild feared sensation—brief spinning, stair walking, or breathing through a narrow straw only when appropriate.
Predict what will happen, induce the sensation briefly, and observe recovery without usual calming it.

win: ✓ I predicted the sensation, borrowed it briefly, and watched my body recover.
supports: Gently exhale after “Test Sensation”; no forcing.
I can use “Test Sensation” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Select Medically → Test Sensation
safety:
PAUSE
Obtain professional and medical guidance before body-sensation exposure, especially with health conditions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DESIGN THE SURPRISE
goal: A practice round works when reality breaks the prediction.

steps.action: Picture the strongest testable prediction in visible terms.
Build a safe practice round aimed at that exact claim, not merely at feeling anxious.
Afterward, keep the original prediction, what occurred, and what the old model cannot easily explain.

win: ✓ What I feel and what is true are separate lanes again.
supports: Exhale after “Picture Outcome”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Build Safe” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Picture Strongest → Build Safe → Picture Outcome
safety:
PAUSE
Redesign rather than intensify when the test cannot fairly evaluate the belief.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PENDULUM BETWEEN TWO TRUTHS
goal: Regulation can be built by travelling, not staying still.

steps.action: Find one activated region and another settled or supported area.
Touch the difficult region with attention for a few seconds, then move to the resource.
Travel back and forth at a pace that preserves choice.
Finish on whichever location offers steadier awareness of your location.

win: ✓ Certainty remained unavailable; movement did not.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Whichever”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Move Resource” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Find Activated → Move Resource → Travel → Finish Whichever
safety:
PAUSE
Stop crossing if each visit amplifies distress rather than returning balance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WAIT FOR THE WHOLE BODY ANSWER
goal: Some experience forms before it can be explained.

steps.action: Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
Leave the answer unpolished.

win: ✓ The body answered before language polished it.
supports: Exhale after “Leave It Raw”; leave it unanswered.
“Leave It Raw”: what changed from “Bring Mind”?
I can use “Ask Body” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Bring Mind → Ask Body → Check Whether → Leave It Raw
safety:
PAUSE
End the inquiry if bodily attention creates panic, numbness, or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
goal: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.

steps.action: Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
Observe whether the body receives an ending.

win: ✓ The urge peaked without becoming a contract.
supports: Exhale after “Observe Whether”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Let Unfold” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Small → Let Unfold → Stop Completion → Observe Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Never direct movement toward a person or continue if aggression escalates.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE BODY’S WORKABLE DISTANCE
goal: Boundaries can be measured before they are argued.

steps.action: Using an object, doorway, or trusted person with consent, test near and far in small increments.
Notice breath, posture, urge, and clarity at each point.
Notice where the body can stay present and communicate.
That distance is data, not a permanent verdict.

win: ✓ The body found a workable distance without turning it into a verdict.
supports: Exhale after “Set Workable Distance”; let wanting crest.
“Set Workable Distance”: what changed from “Use Object”?
I can use “Breath” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Use Object → Breath → Body → Set Workable Distance
safety:
PAUSE
Stop immediately if consent changes or the exercise feels threatening.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE FLOOR
goal: Let external support do part of the holding.

steps.action: Choose one contact point—feet, seat, back, forearms, or hands.
Increase pressure slightly, then release extra effort and notice what the surface continues to carry.
Name its texture, temperature, and steadiness.
You need not manufacture a sense of ground.

win: ✓ The present regained enough detail to hold me.
supports: Exhale after “Trust Ground”; notice the room.
I can use “Release Extra” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose Contact → Release Extra → Name Texture → Trust Ground
safety:
PAUSE
Change position if pressure causes pain, numbness, or restricted circulation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CATCH THE RECOVERY SIGNAL
goal: Settling deserves as much attention as alarm.

steps.action: After body alarm, watch for a swallow, sigh, warmth, trembling, yawn, moisture in the eyes, breath shift, or muscle release.
When one appears, name it accurately and stay with its after-effect.
Do not provoke more.
Teach the mind what recovery looks like.

win: ✓ The alarm stayed loud, but the world got wider.
supports: Exhale after “Look Like”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Name Accurately” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Watch Swallow → Name Accurately → No Extra Trigger → Look Like
safety:
PAUSE
Seek care if shaking, breathing changes, or other symptoms seem medically concerning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE BODY FILE
goal: Do not close the file while the body is still asking for attention.

steps.action: Scan from head to feet for remaining body alarm.
Select the strongest residue and give it one stabilising response: support, movement, warmth, grounding in the present, or rest.
Rescan only once.
State what is complete today and what belongs to later care.

win: ✓ Sensation became data instead of a verdict.
supports: Gently exhale after “State Today”; orient to now.
I can use “Select Strongest” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Scan Head → Select Strongest → Rescan → State Today
safety:
PAUSE
Seek help if the scan uncovers severe symptoms or increasing destabilisation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE BUSY HALF
goal: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.

steps.action: Observe three ordinary cycles.
Rate inhale effort and exhale release separately.
Which phase is working too hard?
Ease only that side toward neutral—less pulling in or less pushing out—while leaving timing alone.
Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.

win: ✓ Comparison lost its right to set my value.
supports: Exhale after “Check Whether”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Rate Inhale” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Observe Ordinary → Rate Inhale → Phase → Leave Timing → Check Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Stop adjustment at the first sign of dizziness, strain, or breath fixation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ALTERNATE THE AIRWAY
goal: Move attention left and right until state feels organised.

steps.action: Sit comfortably.
Without force, close one nostril and breathe through the other; switch sides for the next gentle cycle.
Continue alternating with an unhurried hand.
Keep the breath quiet and abandon retention.
Finish with both sides open and let breathing return to normal.

win: ✓ Left, right, centre: attention finished organised and unforced.
supports: Gently exhale after “Open Both Sides”; no forcing.
I can use “Close Nostril” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Sit Easy → Close Nostril → Continue Unhurried → Keep Breath → Open Both Sides
safety:
PAUSE
Skip when congested, dizzy, breath-sensitive, or advised against the practice.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: VIBRATION ON THE WAY OUT
goal: Let sound carry the exhale without squeezing it.

steps.action: Take an ordinary inhale.
Hum at a soft, comfortable pitch as air leaves, feeling vibration in lips, face, or chest.
Stop before empty.
Listen to the silence after the hum, then decide whether another round would still feel kind.

win: ✓ The current moment has edges again.
supports: Exhale after “Listen Silence”; then keep moving.
I can use “Leave Feeling” before motivation.
formula_flow: Take Ordinary → Leave Feeling → Stop Empty → Listen Silence
safety:
PAUSE
Cease with pain, coughing, light-headedness, or vocal discomfort.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COOL AIR, WARM DECISION
goal: Borrow a settling cue from temperature.

steps.action: Shape the lips or tongue only if comfortable, notice a mild stream of cool air, and let exhalation leave naturally through the nose.
Notice coolness rather than volume.
Stop after a few easy cycles and choose one unhurried action.

win: ✓ Cooling changed the body volume before the mind wrote the explanation.
supports: Exhale after “End After”; notice the room.
I can use “Coolness” to return here.
formula_flow: Imagine Mild → Coolness → End After
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid in cold sensitivity, unsuitable weather, breathing conditions, or discomfort.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE RETURN REP
goal: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.

steps.action: Select one neutral anchor.
Each time distraction appears, notice where attention went and escort it back without commentary.
Count returns rather than uninterrupted seconds.
Finish after ten honest comebacks, even if focus never felt perfect.

win: ✓ Ten returns happened. Perfect focus was never required.
supports: Exhale after “End After”; release the score.
formula_flow: Select Neutral → Attention → Count Rather → End After
safety:
PAUSE
Choose a broader practice if narrow focus increases agitation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET DARKNESS BE COMPLETE
goal: Visual absence does not need a replacement image.

steps.action: In a safe darkened setting, notice darkness as the actual visual field.
When the mind manufactures shapes or stories, recognise image production and return to the unfilled field.
Stay briefly, then reintroduce light on purpose.

win: ✓ Darkness stayed complete for a moment; light returned by choice.
supports: One exhale after “Stay Briefly”; redirect attention.
I can use “Return Unfilled” amid noise.
formula_flow: Set Darkness → Return Unfilled → Stay Briefly
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this practice if darkness triggers panic, trauma, or perceptual disturbance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BEFORE THE SENTENCE
goal: Look for thought at the moment of assembly.

steps.action: Hold attention quietly and wait.
When a thought begins, notice its earliest form: pressure, fragment, image, word, or felt orientation in space.
Do not chase backward after it fully forms.
Simply Notice ‘birth’ and let the completed thought continue.

win: ✓ I caught the instant before the sentence became a story.
supports: One exhale after “Catch the Birth”; redirect attention.
formula_flow: Hold Attention → Earliest → No Backtracking → Catch the Birth
safety:
PAUSE
Choose a visible anchor when vigilant waiting increases tension.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
goal: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.

steps.action: Select one naturally occurring thought.
Stay with its exact wording or image as it alters, fragments, loses relevance, or is replaced.
Spot the first instant when no trace can be found.
Do not resurrect it to verify the ending.

win: ✓ The thought ended. I did not drag it back for an encore.
supports: Exhale after “Let It End”; loosen the label.
I can use “Stay Wording” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Select Naturally → Stay Wording → Identify Instant → Let It End
safety:
PAUSE
End observation if tracking becomes obsessive or exhausting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE RETURN CHAIN
goal: Ongoing sense is built from linked renewals.

steps.action: Choose one attentional act small enough to repeat daily.
Define its cue, duration, and one tiny restart signal.
Each session begins with the final second of yesterday’s intention: ‘return again.’ Protect repetition from heroic increases.
A chain is made of modest links.

win: ✓ I built the return out of small links instead of one heroic comeback.
supports: One exhale after “Link the Return”; redirect attention.
I can use “Set Cue” amid noise.
formula_flow: Choose Attention → Set Cue → Return Repetition → Link the Return
safety:
PAUSE
Reduce frequency if ongoing sense crowds out sleep, duties, or flexibility.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN THE OUTCOME
goal: Effort is yours; total control was never issued.

steps.action: Name the action within your responsibility.
Name the result you cannot command.
Offer the second to God, life, reality, community, or a principle larger than ego—using language authentic to you.
Then do the first with full care.

win: ✓ Gave the outcome back and kept the quality of my action.
supports: Exhale after “Return the Outcome”; slow the clock.
I can use “Name Result” without rushing.
formula_flow: Name Action → Name Result → Use Language → Return the Outcome
safety:
PAUSE
Choose secular release if spiritual framing creates conflict or coercion.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TRACE THE FIRST SPARK
goal: Find what started the fluctuation before content took over.

steps.action: Take one recurring state and move backward through its chain: current thought, preceding sensation, image, memory, external cue, and hidden tendency.
Stop at the earliest condition you can really spot.
Notice the point where future interruption could happen.

win: ✓ The spark became visible early enough to interrupt next time.
supports: Exhale after “Mark the Spark”; let feeling settle.
“Take Recurring” to “Mark the Spark”: what loosened?
I can use “Stop Earliest” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Take Recurring → Stop Earliest → Mark the Spark
safety:
PAUSE
Do not force inaccessible memories or invent causes to complete the chain.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NOT THIS, STILL HERE
goal: Remove identities without attacking experience.

steps.action: Notice body, sensation, thought, emotion, and role in turn.
For each say, ‘Observed—therefore not the whole observer.’ Do not claim they are unreal.
After the sequence, rest with what remains unlabelled, then reconnect to name and place.

win: ✓ The present reclaimed one clear channel.
supports: Exhale after “Rest Unlabelled”; notice the room.
I can use “Keep Perspective” to return here.
formula_flow: Body → Keep Perspective → Rest Unlabelled
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid negation practices during feeling unreal or disconnected, psychosis, or unstable self-experience.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLEAN ACTION, OPEN HANDS
goal: Own the quality of the move, not the universe’s reply.

steps.action: Define what right action looks like in process terms: honest words, careful preparation, timely follow-through.
Specify the outcome you hope for, then place it outside the scoring system.
Judge today only by whether the action met its standard.

win: ✓ I did the clean action and left the outcome with open hands.
supports: Exhale after “Judge the Action”; slow the clock.
I can use “Place Outside” without rushing.
formula_flow: Look Like → Place Outside → Judge the Action
safety:
PAUSE
Results still matter when they reveal harm, error, or a need to change course.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE FEED BEFORE CRAVING VOTES
goal: Restraint works earlier than willpower.

steps.action: Spot the cue that repeatedly captures a sense—screen, smell, image, taste, location.
Set a concrete contact limit before practice round: duration, distance, quantity, or block.
Leave while choice is still available, not after bargaining begins.

win: ✓ I left before craving got a chance to negotiate.
supports: Exhale after “Leave Choice”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Set Concrete” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Identify Cue → Set Concrete → Leave Choice
safety:
PAUSE
Use specialist support for substance use, eating disorders, or compulsions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
goal: One exception is enough to weaken inevitability.

steps.action: Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.

win: ✓ The pattern already has an exception; inevitability just lost ground.
supports: Gently exhale after “Transplant Edge”; no forcing.
I can use “Find Misses” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Name Pattern → Find Misses → Compare Conditions → Transplant Edge
safety:
PAUSE
Exceptions do not make unsafe situations safe; do not use this game to blame yourself for trauma, illness, abuse, discrimination, or coercion.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EFFORT IS STILL AVAILABLE
goal: Spiritual acceptance should not disguise preventable passivity.

steps.action: Name what cannot be changed today.
Beside it, name the smallest domain where effort remains possible.
Take one concrete step there before returning to contemplation.
Let action answer the part of the problem that is actually yours.

win: ✓ Acceptance stopped disguising the part that still needs action.
supports: Exhale after “Let Action”; keep the compass.
I can use “Name Smallest” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Name Cannot → Name Smallest → Take Concrete → Let Action
safety:
PAUSE
Do not frame incapacity, disability, or exhaustion as moral failure.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RUN THE START GATE TWICE
goal: The first start can be rehearsal; the second one becomes real.

steps.action: Choose the opening movements: open the file, place the tool, find the line, or position your hands. Keep it under ten seconds.
do that sequence once without producing work. Stop at the edge of action; this is the dry launch.
Return your hands or screen to neutral exactly once. Leave the plan unchanged or add another rehearsal.
Repeat the same sequence and continue straight into thirty seconds of real work.

win: ✓ The pain kept its truth while life kept another department open.
supports: Exhale after “Live Entry”; keep the compass.
I can use “Dry Launch” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Stage Door → Dry Launch → Full Reset → Live Entry
safety:
PAUSE
Do not rehearse machinery, driving, hazardous tools, or any start sequence that requires formal safety checks.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DIFFERENCE INSIDE ONE FIELD
goal: Diversity need not become division.

steps.action: Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence.
Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
Then include the shared field in which both are present.
Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation.

win: ✓ Difference stayed visible; separation never became necessary.
supports: Exhale after “Let Difference”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Hold Distinct” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Contrasting → Hold Distinct → Include Shared → Let Difference
safety:
PAUSE
Use ordinary distinctions when boundaries or safety require clear separation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE REVERSIBLE DOOR
goal: When uncertain, buy information without buying a prison.

steps.action: Find the smallest action that tests the direction and can be undone: trial, prototype, conversation, temporary booking, one-week schedule.
Name the exit cost and the fact the step could reveal.
Choose the door that returns with data.

win: ✓ The door opened into data, not a prison.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Door”; end the lap.
I can use “Name Exit” without another lap.
formula_flow: Find Smallest → Name Exit → Choose Door
safety:
PAUSE
Do not treat apparently reversible steps as harmless without checking consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WORRY HAS OFFICE HOURS
goal: Give concern an appointment so it stops running reception.

steps.action: Picture the worry exactly and schedule a specific review window later today.
Until then, add only really new facts to the Notice; no live analysis.
At the appointment, decide: act, plan, accept, or discard.
Close on time even if certainty is absent.

win: ✓ The replay lost another lap.
supports: Exhale after “Close Time”; end the lap.
I can use “Add Genuinely” without another lap.
formula_flow: Picture Worry → Add Genuinely → Decide Accept → Close Time
safety:
PAUSE
Use immediate action for urgent safety or time-sensitive problems.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ROTATE THE CHAIR
goal: One perspective is data, not the whole room.

steps.action: Describe the event from your position.
Move seats and say what the other person might perceive, labelling guesses.
Stand as a neutral observer and keep only observable behaviour.
Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.

win: ✓ The conversation gained structure instead of more force.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Future”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Move Seats” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Describe Event → Move Seats → Watch Behaviour → Ask Future
safety:
PAUSE
Skip the other-person chair if it invites self-blame after abuse.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
goal: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.

steps.action: Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.

win: ✓ I found the word carrying the weight and stopped rehearsing the whole sentence.
supports: Gently exhale after “Keep Signal”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Shift Stress” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Say Alarm → Shift Stress → Find Weight → Keep Signal
safety:
PAUSE
Use silent emphasis if speaking is unsafe; stop for voice strain, breathing difficulty, or rising panic.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
goal: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.

steps.action: Choose an object, date, location, and act of remembrance.
Say the name of what was lost, honour what remains meaningful, and name a farewell to what cannot continue.
Close by deciding how the bond or value will be carried forward.

win: ✓ A meaningful next step survived the heaviness.
supports: Exhale after “Close Bond”; keep the compass.
I can use “Say Name” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Choose Object → Say Name → Close Bond
safety:
PAUSE
Seek grief or crisis support when mourning makes safety or functioning difficult.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE OBJECT, MARK THE RELEASE
goal: Let matter carry a decision the mind keeps reopening.

steps.action: Picture or select a safe symbol for what you are relinquishing.
Choose a transformation that fits: fold, seal, store, shred, bury where lawful, or dissolve safely.
Name what is ending and what responsibility remains.
Complete the physical change once.

win: ✓ The object changed once; the decision got a physical full stop.
supports: Exhale after “Mark the Release”; soften the jaw.
“Mark the Release”: what changed from “Picture Safe”?
I can use “Choose Transformation” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Safe → Choose Transformation → Name Responsibility → Mark the Release
safety:
PAUSE
Never burn, bury, ingest, or destroy items unsafely or illegally.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON
goal: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.

steps.action: Ask how far ahead consequences can meaningfully alter today’s move: tonight, one week, six months.
Imagine a line at that horizon.
Park every scenario beyond it unless it changes a present safety or commitment fact.
Decide using information inside the line.

win: ✓ The decision stayed inside today’s useful horizon.
supports: Exhale after “Decide Information”; end the lap.
I can use “Imagine Line” without another lap.
formula_flow: Ask Far → Imagine Line → Park Scenario → Decide Information
safety:
PAUSE
Extend the horizon for hard to undo actions or long-term obligations.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN THE LABEL INTO MOTION
goal: Turn the label into a process you can interrupt.

steps.action: Take the identity or label word dominating the moment.
Translate it into active, time-specific verbs ending in -ing: withdrawing, scanning, grieving, protecting, predicting.
Ask what starts, strengthens, interrupts, and ends that process.

win: ✓ The noun lost its cage; motion exposed a change point.
supports: Exhale after “Ask Strengthens”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Translate Active” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Take Identity → Translate Active → Ask Strengthens
safety:
PAUSE
Do not discard formal diagnoses needed for treatment or access to support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MEANING ON HOLD
goal: Meaning must wait for independent witnesses.

steps.action: Hold the event without explaining it.
Find three facts from different channels—what was said, what was observed, what occurred over time.
Until all three exist, name every meaning temporary.
Then assign the narrowest meaning supported.

win: ✓ I put meaning on hold until the facts had enough witnesses.
supports: Exhale after “Assign Narrowest”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Find Facts” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Hold Event → Find Facts → Name Meaning → Assign Narrowest
safety:
PAUSE
Do not postpone action when even one fact confirms urgent danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE WORD, ONE BREATH, RELEASE
goal: Compress the noise without pretending it is solved.

steps.action: Choose a temporary word that holds the issue: betrayal, pressure, uncertainty, loss.
Say it once during a natural breath, feel its weight, and let the word leave with the breath’s end.
Do not replace it with a second Name for thirty seconds.

win: ✓ One word rode one breath, then left without needing a replacement.
supports: Exhale after “Keep One Name”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Say During” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Choose Temporary → Say During → Keep One Name
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid compression when important complexity must be communicated.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: GIVE THE FORECAST EDGES
goal: A vague fear cannot lose because it never defines a result.

steps.action: Sharpen the prediction with who, what visible event, exact time window, location, and clear threshold.
Define the sign of the event not happening.
Set a review date and refuse to score the prediction before then.

win: ✓ One feared ending just got competition.
supports: Exhale after “Set Review”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Define” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Sharpen Forecast → Define → Set Review
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use precision to obsessively monitor low-stakes uncertainty.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
goal: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.

steps.action: Spot the loudest recall channel—image, sound, touch, smell.
Reduce its brightness, volume, proximity, or texture slightly.
At the same time, strengthen neutral present-day context: the room layout, today’s date, your clothing, or a distant sound.

win: ✓ Memory lost the whole screen; the present regained channels.
supports: Exhale after “Anchor the Present”; keep both sides.
“Anchor the Present”: what changed from “Identify Loudest”?
I can use “Reduce Brightness” before concluding.
formula_flow: Identify Loudest → Reduce Brightness → Anchor the Present

PAUSE
Do not manipulate testimony or use this when precise recall is legally important.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
goal: A useful warning does not require a ruined identity or world.

steps.action: Name the specific lesson the event genuinely supports.
Notice the global conclusion attached to it: ‘Nobody is safe,’ ‘I am weak,’ ‘Life is over,’ or another all-life verdict.
Ask whether the specific lesson still works without the global verdict. Keep what teaches; delete what condemns.

win: ✓ The lesson stayed. The life sentence was deleted.
supports: Exhale after “Separate Them”; keep both sides.
I can use “Spot Verdict” before concluding.
formula_flow: Picture Specific → Picture Global
safety:
PAUSE
Do not dilute lessons that accurately identify continuing danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SET THE LIMIT BEFORE THE NEXT TEST
goal: Decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.

steps.action: Define the behaviour in terms a camera could Keep.
Choose the count, duration, or date that will Notice the limit.
Attach one consequence under your control, such as ending the call, leaving, or changing access.
If the threshold is crossed, follow the contract once without holding a motive trial.

win: ✓ The boundary was decided in calm, so motive did not get a retrial.
supports: Exhale after “Follow Contract”; release extra load.
I can use “Set Threshold” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Count Pattern → Set Threshold → Link Consequence → Follow Contract
safety:
PAUSE
Leave immediately instead of counting repetitions when there is intimidation, violence, or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COME BACK FROM THEIR IMAGINED HEAD
goal: Attention belongs first to what can be known.

steps.action: Picture three boxes: KNOWN, INFERRED, UNKNOWABLE.
Move every claim about the other person into its correct box.
Choose one direct question or boundary based on known facts.
Leave the unknowable box empty of action.

win: ✓ What I know became actionable; what I cannot know stayed empty.
supports: Exhale after “Leave Unknowable”; release extra load.
What lost power: “Sort Three Boxes” → “Leave Unknowable”?
I can use “Move Claim” without carrying it all.

title: SOFT JAW, SAME BOUNDARY
goal: Reduce aggression preparation without weakening the sentence.

steps.action: Notice jaw pressure before speaking.
Separate the teeth, relax the tongue, and exhale naturally.
Deliver the exact limit you planned—no extra smile, apology, or attack.
Let articulation stay clear while muscular threat signalling drops.

win: ✓ The boundary kept its strength after the body dropped the threat pose.
supports: Exhale after “Let Articulation”; release extra load.
I can use “Separate Teeth” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Notice Jaw → Separate Teeth → Deliver Limit → Let Articulation

PAUSE
Stop the conversation if safety or self-control is deteriorating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FINISH THE BODY'S FULL STOP
goal: Let leftover readiness complete one harmless ending.

steps.action: While safely seated, locate one area that still feels ready to push, brace, turn, or withdraw.
Choose a pain-free direction and add only light self-resistance.
Complete the movement slowly once, then release all effort rather than repeating it.
Compare resting pressure, movement range, and urge before and after.

win: ✓ Leftover readiness completed its harmless ending and stopped asking for more.
supports: Exhale after “Check Neutral”; mark the pause.
I can use “Add Resistance” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Find Readiness → Add Resistance → Complete Slowly → Check Neutral

PAUSE
Stop immediately with pain, dizziness, numbness, injury risk, or uncertain movement.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE ACTIVE SLOT
goal: Short-term attention needs a deliberate admission policy.

steps.action: Create three positions: ACTIVE, WAITING, ARCHIVE.
Put only one concern in active, one likely next item in waiting, and route everything else to archive with a retrieval Notice.
Give the active concern a protected time box.

win: ✓ Attention admitted one concern and gave the rest a booked return time.
supports: Exhale after “Give Active”; mark the pause.
I can use “Wait Route” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Create Positions → Wait Route → Give Active
safety:
PAUSE
Expand active capacity only when parallel monitoring is genuinely required.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE POINT OF NO MORE INFLUENCE
goal: The body needs to know when available action is complete.

steps.action: Name what you have already done, what remains unknown, and which outcomes no longer respond to effort.
Notice the exact boundary where influence ends.
Use one physical closing action and redirect into a present responsibility.

win: ✓ Available action reached its edge; the body got permission to close.
supports: Exhale after “Use Physical”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Boundary” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Remain Unknown → Boundary → Use Physical

PAUSE
Re-enter action if genuinely new controllable information appears.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE MENTAL TOOL, NOT THE PRESSURE
goal: Wrong mental mode makes effort repeat itself.

steps.action: Classify the demand as SOLVE, DECIDE, FEEL, ACCEPT, COMMUNICATE, or WAIT.
Name the mode currently running.
Shut it down and do the first action belonging to the correct mode—calculate, choose, allow, release, speak, or schedule.

win: ✓ I changed mental tools instead of pushing the wrong one harder.
supports: Gently exhale after “Choose Shut”; orient to now.
I can use “Name Mode” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Decide Accept → Name Mode → Choose Shut

PAUSE
Mixed situations may need modes in sequence rather than one label.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DEMOTE THE HEADLINE EXPERIENCE
goal: Foreground and background can share equal status.

steps.action: Hold the dominant sensation or thought with three background what you notices—one sound, one contact point, one visual feature.
For a contained interval, give all four equal attentional weight without imagining a separate watcher.
Notice how centrality changes.

win: ✓ Headline demoted. The background gets equal screen time now.
